title_block.title: NM08 Paired Liver Systems
title_block.subtitle: Microsomal CLint and Hepatocyte depletion CLint — Final report R1
lines: Dr M. Larkin, DMPK Study Director

blocks.p: The NM08 test article set comprised {{PRJ0055:n_compounds}} compounds. The study opened on 06/05/2006, an interim interpretation was issued on 06/26/2006, and this report closes the paired liver-system work on 07/18/2006. Human and rat matrices are reported separately; neither species is substituted for the other in the progression assessment.
Nimbravelle advanced the analogues whose slower hepatocyte turnover agreed with their microsomal ranking. This is a relative in vitro selection, not a prediction of measured circulating exposure.

Table 2 gives Microsomal CLint at 0.5 mg/mL protein and 1 µM test article. Clearance is expressed in µL/min/mg; the associated depletion half-life is expressed in minutes. Human and rat columns must be read within their respective matrix.

table.caption: Table 2. Microsomal CLint and depletion half-life

blocks.p: Half-life and intrinsic clearance describe the same depletion experiment and are not independent confirmation of activity. The matrix basis differs from the cell-normalized results that follow.

Table 3 presents Hepatocyte depletion CLint in human and rat cryopreserved hepatocytes, at 1 µM and 0.5×10^6 cells/mL. Results are expressed in µL/min/10^6 cells. Comparison with Table 2 is by within-system ranking rather than subtraction of the printed clearance values.

table.caption: Table 3. Hepatocyte depletion CLint by species

blocks.p: A slower whole-cell depletion profile supports retention within this test article set when its direction agrees with the microsomal assessment. Whole-cell turnover also depends on access to the intracellular compartment.

The exposure gate addressed whether the aminotriazine analogues retained a consistent metabolic stability advantage across an isolated enzyme-rich matrix and an intact cellular matrix. The design does not isolate a particular metabolic enzyme or establish the pathway responsible for parent loss.

No plasma binding, transport, solubility or in vivo exposure result is supplied by this study. Those properties cannot be inferred from a favorable clearance ranking. The report therefore confines its recommendation to the paired liver systems.

The controlling accession is {{PRJ0055:lims_id}}. Compound identifiers printed in Tables 2 and 3 are the link between the analytical record and the NM08 test article set. The accompanying assay worksheet holds the accession-lot mapping; identifiers must be carried intact into any later exposure-gate record.

The report uses the submitted parent identity as its analyte designation. It does not replace identity or purity characterization. An apparently favorable depletion profile cannot resolve a mismatch between the submitted material and its intended structure.

table.caption: Table 4. Matrix basis used throughout this report

blocks.p: Microsomal clearance is protein-normalized and hepatocyte clearance is cell-normalized. Conversion between these bases would require additional physiological scaling assumptions. None is applied here. A human result is not a quantitative rat surrogate, even when the direction of ranking agrees.

Microsomal incubations used 0.5 mg/mL protein and 1 µM test article. Timed aliquots were quenched for parent analysis. The depletion assessment considers the interpretable interval of the parent signal and the corresponding matrix controls, rather than treating every terminal sample as informative.

Loss unrelated to metabolic turnover must be considered when interpreting the series. Protein association, handling loss and matrix-dependent signal response can contribute to apparent depletion. Microsomal CLint is reported as an operational result under the stated incubation conditions.

Hepatocyte incubations used 1 µM test article and 0.5×10^6 cells/mL. Human and rat preparations were evaluated independently. Parent depletion was normalized to the cell basis used in Table 3; that basis is retained in the captions and in the conclusion.

The intact-cell experiment incorporates entry into cells as well as intracellular turnover. Slow apparent clearance can reflect restricted access as well as metabolic stability. Agreement with microsomal ordering supports the selection but does not remove this limitation.

Javier Quintana's mass-spectrometry review covers the parent-analyte measurement used for the depletion interpretation. The analyte card and assay worksheet remain the controlling records for sample assignment, acquisition details and integration decisions. This report presents the derived clearance tables rather than a reproduction of individual chromatograms.

Matrix-associated response changes must be distinguished from time-dependent loss of parent. A signal that cannot be interpreted within the analytical response range is not evidence of complete metabolic disappearance.

The supplied result record does not provide numerical quantitation limits, calibration range or individual terminal-sample concentrations. Those values are therefore not asserted in this report. The tables support comparison of derived clearance; they do not support a claim that every terminal sample was quantifiable.

Where depletion approaches the measurement floor, late samples may cease to support the fitted interval. Where little parent loss occurs, the observation window limits resolution of slower turnover. Both constraints matter when interpreting close rankings, and neither justifies adding precision beyond the reported table.

Helen Marchwood's matrix acceptance review is linked to the assay worksheet dated 07/18/2006. Acceptance is considered by system and species. A satisfactory record in human microsomes cannot release rat hepatocyte samples or resolve an unrelated matrix response concern.

list: Retain accession-lot identity through sample assignment.
Read the depletion interval alongside the applicable matrix record.
Keep species and normalization basis visible in the released result.
Escalate ambiguous parent loss before using it as a progression argument.

blocks.p: No compound-specific acceptance exception is identified in the supplied final result tables. This statement is limited to the report dataset: it does not constitute an independent assertion that every underlying analytical sample passed an unreported numerical criterion.

The analytical-limit qualifications in Section 10 apply to the entire interpretation. The report does not invent sample exclusions, repeat runs or a numerical acceptance threshold. Any subsequent correction to the controlling assay worksheet should be assessed for its effect on the relevant species ranking before this report is reused.

The depletion approach interprets parent loss over time under the stated matrix loading. Intrinsic clearance is an incubation-derived descriptor. Its comparison assumes consistent treatment of analyte identity, interpretable signal interval and matrix normalization across the test article set.

The half-life columns in the microsomal table must remain paired with their corresponding species clearance columns. Rounding can obscure small differences. It would be inappropriate to infer an additional significant digit, or to re-rank close entries using a rounded half-life alone.

The human columns provide the primary paired-system comparison for this exposure gate. Read the human microsomal ordering first, then ask whether the human hepatocyte profile supports the same direction. A favorable result in only one system calls for qualification rather than an automatic stability claim.

The conclusion records the client's selection of analogues with agreement between slower hepatocyte turnover and microsomal ranking. It does not supply a new numerical pass threshold or identify a potency trade-off, because neither is contained in this study record.

Rat results provide a separate species context for the NM08 set. They should be retained alongside human findings when planning later exposure work. Concordance can support a coherent follow-up rationale; discordance should remain visible rather than being averaged away.

These rat in vitro tables do not establish rat exposure, oral availability or dose selection. Any later in vivo study would need its own route, formulation, sampling and bioanalytical record. No such result is included in this final report.

A direct arithmetic comparison of µL/min/mg with µL/min/10^6 cells has no defined meaning without a scaling model. The paired-system decision instead asks whether the relative direction of parent turnover agrees. The separate result tables preserve the evidence needed to revisit that judgment.

Agreement strengthens the case for retaining an analogue within this test article set; it does not prove a common rate-limiting process. Disagreement can be scientifically useful, indicating that cellular access or additional metabolic capacity may matter to interpretation.

Nimbravelle advanced the analogues whose slower hepatocyte turnover agreed with their microsomal ranking. Megan Larkin records that decision as the study outcome for Nimbravelle Medicines Inc. The decision rests on the matrix-specific tables and the qualifications stated above.

Later exposure-gate discussions should cite {{PRJ0055:project_id}} and preserve the original compound identifiers. The present recommendation is not a guarantee of systemic exposure or a replacement for the further characterization required by the client.

This R1 final report is dated 07/18/2006. The related MV-2006-090_AssayWorksheet_071806_v03.xls contains the accession-lot mapping, matrix acceptance checks and paired assay results. The final report is the narrative interpretation; the worksheet is the accompanying structured assay record.

The interim communication of 06/26/2006 is superseded for final interpretation by this report. Corrections should retain the study and accession identifiers and explicitly state whether the released ranking or progression decision changes.

list: Parent depletion is interpreted under the incubation conditions shown with each result table.
Microsomal and hepatocyte units are not interchangeable.
No physiological scaling or exposure prediction is applied.
Unreported quantitation limits and sample-level acceptance outcomes are not supplied by inference.

blocks.p: These assumptions travel with any extract from the result tables. Removing them would broaden the apparent claim beyond the work performed.
